title: Marked formal objects and versal rings at a stack point
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with an $R$-algebra structure, and let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] [def-pc-scheme], with fibred-groupoid and scheme-test conventions as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Fix $x\in\mathcal X(\operatorname{Spec}k)$. Write $\mathcal X(A)$ for the fibre on the affine $R$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}A$; a morphism over $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ encodes the pullback identification. A complete marked local $R$-algebra is a commutative Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(C,\mathfrak m_C)$ [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] with an $R$-algebra isomorphism $C/\mathfrak m_C\cong k$, complete for its maximal-ideal-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Here local means having a unique maximal ideal. A marked formal object over $C$ consists of objects $\eta_n\in\mathcal X(C/\mathfrak m_C^n)$ for every integer $n\geq1$, coherent transition isomorphisms for every reduction from a higher positive level to a lower one (identity and composition agree), and markings $\eta_n|_k\cong x$ commuting with all transitions. A test algebra is an Artinian local $R$-algebra $A$ with a specified $R$-algebra isomorphism $A/\mathfrak m_A\cong k$; Artinian means that descending chains of ideals stabilize. A map $f:A\to B$ between local rings is local if $f^{-1}(\mathfrak m_B)=\mathfrak m_A$. Test maps are local $R$-maps inducing the identity on the specified residue field $k$. For a local residue-preserving $R$-map $v:C\to A$, let $N_A$ be the least positive integer with $\mathfrak m_A^{N_A}=0$, which exists by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent]. Define $\eta_v$ by pullback of $\eta_{N_A}$ along the quotient-induced map $C/\mathfrak m_C^{N_A}\to A$; this map is defined because $v(\mathfrak m_C^{N_A})\subseteq\mathfrak m_A^{N_A}=0$. For any other positive $n$ killed by $v$, the evaluation comparison is the composite of the transition pullback isomorphisms through the common level $\max(n,N_A)$, with pullback composition constraints. All restrictions of evaluations use these comparisons. Such a marked formal object is versal if for every surjection $q:A'\twoheadrightarrow A$ of test algebras, every such $v$, every marked object $\zeta'\in\mathcal X(A')$ with $\zeta'|_k\cong x$, and every marking-preserving isomorphism $\zeta'|_A\cong\eta_v$, there are a local residue-preserving $R$-map $v':C\to A'$ with $qv'=v$ and a marking-preserving isomorphism $\zeta'\cong\eta_{v'}$ whose restriction is the prescribed one. A versal ring at $x$ means such a complete marked local $R$-algebra admitting a versal marked formal object.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q26-59839d1cf (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: This delivery is the item only, a definition with no new nodes and no proof steps; I read it in full. The marked complete Noetherian local algebra, the coherent marked tower and the lifting condition along every surjection of test algebras with the prescribed isomorphism agree with Stacks 0DQV (stacks-geometry.tex:51), artin 0CXJ (artin.tex:1587 and the lifting diagrams after it) and formal-defos 06HR/06HS (formal-defos.tex:2187/2195). Evaluating at N_A, the least positive integer with m_A^N_A=0, is well defined: v is local, so v(m_C^N_A) is contained in m_A^N_A=0. N_A exists by the cited Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent. Other killed levels are compared through max(n,N_A), which agrees with the Lean IsVersal. Edge cases checked: A=k gives N=1, k[e] gives N=2, q=id is consistent, the zero ring is excluded, and automorphisms are kept. The generalised R and k are harmless because the item is a definition; the existence and extension lemmas that use it impose their own Noetherian local and finite-residue hypotheses. def-sfb-artin-deformation-test-category (an abstract cofibred groupoid on C_{R,k}) and def-sfb-pointwise-versal-lifting are related but different notions, so neither is a duplicate. Batch-5 flag: the item cites def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids only for the fibred-groupoid convention. The node it reaches, def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism, is a general definition of projectivity and not a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality. The previous dependency, def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack, already cited the same node, so the closure is unchanged. Unit, chapter, blueprint and Lean record are unchanged. No SGA source is used.
